Audit analytical robustness across a multiverse specification curve

Source: R/audit-multiverse.R
audit_multiverse.Rd

Evaluates a modeling pipeline across the full Cartesian grid of analytical decision forks (e.g., outlier handling, covariate sets, missing-data rules, and estimator choices) following specification-curve / multiverse analysis. Summarizes specification-level estimates, standard errors, confidence intervals, p-values, convergence rates, overall median and interquartile range (IQR), sign consistency, proportion statistically significant (\(p \le \alpha\)), and per-fork variance decomposition (eta_squared) identifying which analytical decision drives fragility.

Usage

audit_multiverse(
  data,
  decisions,
  fit_fn,
  extract_fn = NULL,
  param = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  max_specs = 256L,
  min_sign_consistency_warn = 0.9,
  min_sign_consistency_fail = 0.75,
  max_iqr_ratio_warn = 0.5,
  max_iqr_ratio_fail = 1,
  max_fail_rate = 0.1
)

Arguments

data

Analysis dataset (typically a data.frame) passed as the first argument to fit_fn.

decisions

Non-empty named list of analytical decision forks, where each element is a vector of candidate choices (e.g., list(outliers = c("none", "winsor"), covariates = c("minimal", "full"))).

fit_fn

Function function(data, spec) receiving data and a named list spec specifying one choice per decision fork, and returning either a fitted model (lm, glm, lmerMod, htest), a named list with estimate (and optional se, ci_lower, ci_upper, p_value, converged), or a numeric scalar/vector.

extract_fn

Optional extractor function(fit) returning a named list (estimate, optional se, ci_lower, ci_upper, p_value, converged) or numeric vector. When NULL, statci auto-extracts from standard model objects and lists.

param

Optional character scalar naming the focal parameter to audit when fit_fn returns multiple coefficients (defaults to the first non-intercept parameter).

alpha

Nominal two-sided significance threshold for computing prop_significant and Wald confidence intervals (default 0.05).

max_specs

Maximum allowed Cartesian grid size (default 256L) to prevent accidental combinatorial explosion in CI.

min_sign_consistency_warn

Minimum sign-consistency proportion before emitting "warn" (default 0.90).

min_sign_consistency_fail

Minimum sign-consistency proportion before emitting "fail" (default 0.75).

max_iqr_ratio_warn

Maximum IQR / |median| spread ratio before emitting "warn" (default 0.50).

max_iqr_ratio_fail

Maximum IQR / |median| spread ratio before emitting "fail" (default 1.00).

max_fail_rate

Maximum tolerable specification failure/non-convergence rate before emitting "fail" (default 0.10).

Value

An S3 object of class "statci_multiverse" containing specifications (sorted tibble::tibble), summary (list of overall robustness metrics), fork_sensitivity (tibble::tibble ranking each decision fork by variance explained), decisions, settings, and overall status ("pass", "warn", or "fail").

Examples

set.seed(42)
df <- data.frame(x = rnorm(80), c1 = rnorm(80))
df$y <- 1 + 0.9 * df$x + 0.3 * df$c1 + rnorm(80, sd = 0.6)
mv <- audit_multiverse(
  data = df,
  decisions = list(
    outliers = c("none", "winsor_5pct"),
    covariates = c("bivariate", "adjusted")
  ),
  fit_fn = function(d, spec) {
    if (spec$outliers == "winsor_5pct") {
      qs <- quantile(d$y, c(0.05, 0.95))
      d$y <- pmin(pmax(d$y, qs[1]), qs[2])
    }
    if (spec$covariates == "bivariate") lm(y ~ x, data = d) else lm(y ~ x + c1, data = d)
  },
  param = "x"
)
mv
#> [PASS] statci Multiverse Specification Curve (x: 4/4 valid specs)
#> median = 0.8066, IQR = 0.0841 [min = 0.7434, max = 0.8714]
#> sign consistency = 100.0%, p <= 0.05 = 100.0%, top driver = outliers
